_comment: Policy for agent-authored pull requests. This file is ALWAYS loaded from the merge-base commit, never from the PR head, so a PR cannot relax its own guardrails. Edits here require a human reviewer (see deny_paths: scripts/ci/**).
_allow_paths_comment: tune-database.js is the one executable file on this list. scripts/agent/ingest_tunes.py appends community tune entries to its TUNES array, and the array is the source of truth for the cards, so there is nowhere else for an entry to go on a site with no backend. Three things bound it: the entry is written through tune_db.render_entry, which emits every string via json.dumps and refuses keys outside the known schema; max_changed_lines caps how much of the file one PR can touch; and the PR is still a proposal that a human merges. Widening this list further -- especially to script.js, quadphysics.js, or a glob -- is not a policy tweak, it is handing the agent the site's behaviour.

html_checks._allow_jsonld_comment: Exempts <script type="application/ld+json"> from forbid_inline_script, but only when the block contains valid JSON. Every other inline script stays forbidden, including type="text/javascript". Defaults to true when the key is absent; set false to restore the blanket ban.
html_checks._allow_inline_script_hashes_comment: Exact-content allowlist for inline <script> bodies, keyed by CSP-style sha256-<base64> of the script's text content. Absent or empty means the blanket forbid_inline_script ban applies with no exemptions -- that is the default and it is what should stay true for every page that does not have a documented reason otherwise. The hash is the identity: a pinned script keeps its exemption only while it stays character-for-character what a reviewer read, so one edit makes it an unknown script again and the gate fails with the newly computed hash printed. Line endings are folded to LF and surrounding whitespace is stripped before hashing (CRLF working tree vs LF object store, and reindenting a page should not break CI); internal whitespace is NOT normalised, because that is where something could hide. This is deliberately not keyed on type or filename the way allow_jsonld is -- JSON-LD is inert data a browser never executes, these are executable, and a per-type or per-file rule would exempt any inline script in those files, which is the hole the rule exists to close. Adding an entry here is a security decision and requires a human reviewer (see deny_paths: scripts/ci/**).

allow_inline_script_hashes.sha256-FcuGtowxz5Qysr2TXFpaJMfLuuZ7DyUhS: js-motion pre-paint flag. Sets the class the scroll-reveal styles hang off before first paint so revealed content never flashes in and back out, and only when IntersectionObserver exists so unsupported browsers are never left with hidden content. Must stay inline: as an external file it becomes a render-blocking request before LCP, which is the regression PR #78 fixed. Present in index.html, bench.html, gear.html and tune-database.html -- byte-identical in all four, verified.

bench_schema._comment: Schema for data/bench/<slug>.json files: first-hand measured data for one build, keyed by the build_orphan slug. The generator refuses to write a build_orphan guide unless a file matching this schema exists at origin/main. Same validation style as tune_schema: required fields, numeric ranges, placeholder rejection, and a source that names how the numbers were measured. Flight-time fields: at least one of hover_time_s / cruise_time_s / freestyle_time_s must be present and measured. They are not all required -- a real bench session often yields one flight type first, and demanding the others invites invented numbers, which is the exact failure this gate exists to prevent.
